evals.prompt: Our city council wants us to build an app that tells residents exactly when the next bus will arrive, because bus ridership has dropped 20% in two years. Before we start building, can you check we're even solving the right problem?
evals.expected_output: A Round Peg reframe that exposes 'build an arrival-time app' as a smuggled-in solution, names the underlying need (getting more residents to choose the bus) separately from it, offers a new problem statement that does not presuppose an app, a wildcard framing built with a different lever, a list of what the original frame hid (e.g. non-riders, reliability, route coverage), a cheap test of the frame, and a Handoff block led by the new problem statement.
expectations: The three agents think-round-peg-frame-auditor, think-round-peg-reframer, and think-round-peg-frame-judge were each spawned one after another, in that order, with no step run in parallel
The frame audit names building the app as a smuggled-in solution and states an underlying need (e.g. more residents choosing the bus) that does not mention an app
The reframer returns at least 8 'How might we…' framings, each tagged with a lever, using at least 6 distinct levers
The new problem statement does not presuppose an app or any other specific solution, and the wildcard framing uses a different lever from the primary
The final output ends with a '## Handoff' section whose first bullet carries the new problem statement verbatim

evals.prompt: My manager asked me to 'figure out how to get engineers to write more documentation' because it takes new hires about three months to become productive. I suspect this is an XY problem. Can you reframe it?
evals.expected_output: An XY check that separates Y (more documentation) from X (new hires productive sooner), framings scored on leverage, fidelity, and actionability with the original scored as a control, a primary that stays faithful to faster onboarding, a list of what the original frame excluded (e.g. new hires as stakeholders, pairing, codebase complexity), and no full solution plan.
expectations: The XY check explicitly identifies Y as more documentation and X as new hires becoming productive faster
Every framing is scored on leverage, fidelity, and actionability, and the original framing is scored alongside them as a control
The chosen primary framing still serves the underlying need of faster onboarding, and any framing that drops that need is rejected as a dodge rather than chosen
The output lists what the original frame excluded, naming at least two stakeholders, metrics, or solution classes the 'write more docs' wording ruled out
The skill stops at a new problem statement and a test of the frame, without delivering a full implementation plan for solving it
